claims.source_quote_ar: تحصيل ظلمة هذا في مكان ضياء ذاك وبالعكس.
claims.claim_ar: تِبَاق/مقابلة بين الضّدّين (أصغر/أكبر، فى الأرض/فى السماء) لإظهار شمول علم الله وإحاطته بكل شيء.
claims.claim_en: Antithesis (tibaq/muqabalah) between opposites (small/large, on earth/in the sky) to demonstrate God's exhaustive knowledge and encompassing awareness.
claims.needs_review_reason: The supporting commentary excerpt refers to antithetical formulation (night/day) in another context; applying it to the small/large and earth/sky contrasts in this ayah is an inference and should be double-checked against direct tafsir-balagha sources for this verse.
claims.rhetorical_effect: The juxtaposition of extremes (microscopic to cosmic) intensifies the sense of God's all-encompassing knowledge and leaves no gap for concealment.

claims.claim_ar: استخدام تركيب «مَا ... إِلَّا» للدلالة على الحصر والتقييد (قصر المعنى)، أي: لا يحصل شيء من ذلك إلا وأنتم عليه شهود أو مسجَّل.
claims.claim_en: Use of the 'ma ... illa' construction to indicate restriction/exception (hasr/qasr), confining the stated matters so as to emphasize that nothing occurs outside God's knowledge/recording.
claims.rhetorical_effect: Constricting the scope (by 'ما... إلا') increases emphatic force—what is stated is exhaustive and leaves no exception to God's witnessing and knowledge.

claims.claim_ar: الآية تستعمل أسلوب تقرير واستئناف لإثبات قدرة الله وعلمه بشكل قاطع، فتأتي الجمل متتابعة لتأكيد ذلك.
claims.claim_en: Assertive/resumptive style (asloob hakim): the verse uses resumed/affirmative clauses to decisively assert God's power and knowledge; the sequence of clauses functions to consolidate the doctrinal point.
claims.needs_review_reason: The cited commentary speaks of this stylistic mechanism in a similar Qur'anic context; mapping it to this verse is plausible but should be validated against dedicated balagha commentaries on S10:A61.
claims.rhetorical_effect: The resumed assertions create a cumulative, authoritative tone that strengthens the reader's conviction in the stated divine attributes (power, hearing, seeing, record-keeping).

claims.claim_ar: تكرار أدوات العطف والتوازي («وما ... وما ... ولا ... ولا ...») لتكثيف العرض وإعطاء الآية إيقاعاً بلاغياً موحّداً.
claims.claim_en: Badi' — repetition/parallel coordination: the repeated conjunctions and parallel clauses ('wa-ma ... wa-ma ... wa-la ... wa-la ...') compress and intensify the presentation, producing a unified rhetorical rhythm.
claims.needs_review_reason: The supporting chunk mentions coordination/conjunction in a related exposition; explicit discussion of 'repetition' for this verse is not present in the supplied text, so the identification relies on structural reading of the ayah and should be checked with primary balagha sources.
claims.rhetorical_effect: Repetition and syntactic parallelism create a rhythmic accumulation that impresses the listener and underlines the comprehensiveness of the claim.
